REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - MARCH 23, 2026 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact City of Cerritos ADA/504 Coordinator, Drew Schneider, at (562) 916-1314 at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to public meetings.

Public Comments and Suggestions
This section is reserved for public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and items not listed on the agenda but that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the legislative body. Verbal comments may be limited to three minutes per speaker, subject to the Mayor/Chair extending to a maximum of five minutes per speaker, with a total time allotted not to exceed 45 minutes unless the Mayor/Chair extends.
7.
Consent Calendar
Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the legislative body, there will be no separate discussion of these items. If a legislative body member requests separate consideration, the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

11A.
Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

Closed Session Report
If the City Council adjourns to Closed Session, the City Council/Successor Agency will reconvene into Open Session after its conclusion and designated City staff will provide a verbal report on any reportable action taken. This report will be memorialized in the official meeting minutes.
13.
Adjournment

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MONDAY,
MARCH 23, 2026, 7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Bob De Leon, Calvary Chapel Artesia.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Troop 72.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Lynda P. Johnson
  Mayor/Chair Frank Aurelio Yokoyama

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council honoring:

  Chick-fil-A (Business Spotlight). A video presentation was displayed.

  Assemblywoman Sharon Quirk-Silva, California State Assembly; Amie Stewart,
  Board Member, Bellflower Unified School District; Dr. Dawn Green, President,
  Cerritos College Board of Trustees; Dr. Mariaelena "Meg" Jimenez, Principal,
  Frank C. Leal Elementary; Tatiana Yokoyama Bui, Vice President, ABC Unified
  School District School Board; and Chloe Emmanuelle Luna Mendez and Annabel
  Rose Gandra Tiongson, Co-Directors, Club Kaibigan Pilipino Cultural Night
  (Women's History Month).

  Ny'Kierra Jackson and Julian Espinoza (Cerritos High School 2026 CIF Southern
  Wrestling Champions).

  Maximilian Zamora (Cerritos Senior Center Employee of the Quarter).

5B.  Review and consideration of City Council appointments to the Cerritos Advisory
  Boards (Commissions and Committees) (2025-2027 Term) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Seeing none, the Mayor declared
  the public comments period closed.
 City of Cerritos  Monday, March 23, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 9

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

5B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Hong, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve
  Councilmember Hong’s nomination listed below to serve the remainder of the 2025-
  2027 term, through April 30, 2027 (COUNCIL):

  Name  Advisory Board
  Joan Pylman  City Celebrations Committee

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, administered the oath of office to appointee, Joan Pylman.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Johnson, to approve Mayor
  Yokoyama’s nomination listed below to serve the remainder of the 2025-2027 term,
  through April 30, 2027 (COUNCIL):

  Name  Advisory Board
  Emil Ali  City Celebrations Committee

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, administered the oath of office to appointee, Emil Ali.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Kurtis Forsythe expressed concern regarding the State’s public health policies and
  procedures during the COVID-19 pandemic and submitted documents for the official
  record. (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public meeting are considered
  public record. Public requests for copies of the full-text redacted written
  correspondence can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City
  Clerk.)

  Melissa Raralio Snyder presented two (2) enclosed documents, stating the enclosures
  were Notices of Intention to Circulate a Recall Petition, in accordance with California
  Elections Code Division 11, intended for service upon the Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem.
 City of Cerritos  Monday, March 23, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 9

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Gloria Pulido congratulated the City’s Women’s History Month proclamation recipients
  and expressed recognition of the Mayor’s final meeting as presiding officer of his
  2025-2026 mayoral term.

  Daisy Lagasca inquired regarding recent Citywide special events and individuals
  recognized by the City.

  Murali Vasudevan expressed concern regarding recent City actions and the City’s
  current political climate.

  The Mayor announced that prior to the meeting, the City Council received six (6)
  written comments submitted for Item 6, inclusive of four (4) comments for Item 12,
  for inclusion in the official record. Requests for copies of the written comments
  submitted for this meeting can be made during regular business hours to the Office
  of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Monday, March 9, 2026, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular
  Meeting Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to approve the Monday,
  March 9, 2026, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Financial Reports

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated March 23, 2026 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  March 23, 2026  $4,958,077.70 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Monday, March 23, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 4 of 9

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  Approval of Financial Reports (continued)

7B.2. City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the period ending January
  31, 2026 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to approve City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the period ending January 31, 2026
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.3. Approval of Fiscal Year 2025-26 budget amendments (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to authorize an
  administrative-initiated Fiscal Year (FY) 2025-26 budget amendment in accordance with
  Joint Budget Resolution No. 2025-19/No. CSA 2025-02 and the Strategic Financial Plan
  and Budget Preparation Policy (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  Account/Project: 110-561-63110 Computer Supplies
  Amount: $125,000
  Justification: A budget amendment in the amount of $125,000 is requested for
  citywide software licenses and subscriptions. Additional funding is needed to
  ensure sufficient appropriations are available to cover current-year costs
  associated with software renewals, including subscription-based services related
  to the Tyler Enterprise ERP (EERP) and Enterprise Permitting and Licensing (EPL)
  projects previously approved by the City Council (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Award of contract for the design of the Regional Stormwater Capture Facility at the
  Cerritos Sports Complex, Project No. 22505, RFP No. 1565-25 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $1,855,831 for the design of the Regional
  Stormwater Capture Facility, Project No. 22505, RFP No. 1565-25, to CWE, and
  reject the other proposals; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to execute any project-related
  amendments, up to the approved 10% contingency of $185,583, in
  accordance with the City's adopted Purchasing and Contracting Policy.
  (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  Monday, March 23, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 9

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Continuance of the existence of a local emergency concerning a gasoline leak
  from a privately owned existing pipeline on the Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine public
  golf course, and potential threat to the safety of persons and property requiring
  remediation, repair, and improvement of the public golf course and other City-
  owned public property, as specified (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to:

  1. Continue the local emergency as proclaimed in Resolution No. 2023-05, at the
  Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine Golf Course and the nearby City property containing the
  C-4 well site;

  2. Make the findings set forth in Sections 1 through 8 of Resolution No. 2023-05,
  and incorporate by reference those findings, as they relate to the continued
  existence of a local emergency as specified; and

  3. Direct staff to provide a report to the City Council regarding the local
  emergency at least once every 60 days, pursuant to Section 8630(c) of the
  California Government Code, until the City Council terminates the local
  emergency (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7E.  Standing Agenda Item: Potential consideration of the Swim and Fitness Center
  Rehabilitation Project, Project No. 20201 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to take no action at this
  time and defer consideration of the Swim and Fitness Center boiler replacement
  until such time that the existing boiler system requires replacement (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Monday, March 23, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 9

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Recommendation by the Cerritos Planning Commission, on a vote of 5-0, to
  approve the following:

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and introduce AN ORDINANCE
  OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2026-
  2, A REQUEST TO AMEND TITLE 5 AND TITLE 22 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL
  CODE BY AMENDING CHAPTER 5.35 AND ADDING SECTION 22.40.340 TO
  PROHIBIT THE SALE, DISTRIBUTION, POSSESSION, AND CONSUMPTION OF
  NITROUS OXIDE IN THE CITY OF CERRITOS* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) Guidelines, this project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.

  A staff report was given by Sabrina Chan, Director of Community Development.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments period. Noting no
  individuals elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public hearing
  and the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Yokoyama, to waive full reading
  of and introduce Ordinance No. 1062, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
  APPROVING DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2026-2, A REQUEST TO AMEND
  TITLE 5 AND TITLE 22 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE BY AMENDING
  CHAPTER 5.35 AND ADDING SECTION 22.40.340 TO PROHIBIT THE SALE,
  DISTRIBUTION, POSSESSION, AND CONSUMPTION OF NITROUS OXIDE IN THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of a Freeway Maintenance Agreement by and between the
  City of Cerritos and the California Department of Transportation.

  Review and consideration of a community cleanup event (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Alvin Papa, Director of Public Works/City Engineer.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Seeing none, the Mayor declared the
  public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Hong, to:

  1. Approve the Freeway Maintenance Agreement (FMA) between the City of Cerritos
  and Caltrans for portions of SR-91 and SR-605, and authorize the Mayor and City
  Manager to execute the agreement;
 City of Cerritos  Monday, March 23, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 7 of 9

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  (continued)

  2. Authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to periodically update FMA
  attachments, and take any and all actions as are necessary or advisable to
  implement and administer the FMA; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to coordinate with Caltrans to conduct a Community
  Cleanup Event at a date and location to be determined in accordance with the
  provided safety requirements and within the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 budget as a
  new appropriation (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration to rename the intersection of Shoemaker Avenue and Oak
  Crest Street after Whitney High School founding principal, Robert Beall (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey, Deputy City Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to the potential renaming of the
  intersection at Shoemaker Avenue and Oak Crest Street after Whitney High School
  founding principal, Robert Beall:

  Kirit Chauhan
  Joan Pylman
  Celia Spitzer

  Daisy Lagasca inquired regarding the criteria for renaming an intersection after a
  member of the Cerritos community.

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, announced that prior to the meeting, the City Council
  members received full-text, unredacted copies of the one (1) written comment
  submitted for Item 9B, by the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the
  official record. Requests for copies of the written comments submitted for this
  meeting can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  ORIGINAL MOTION (HELD PENDING): It was moved by Tse, and seconded by
  Johnson, to defer consideration of the renaming the intersection at Shoemaker
  Avenue and Oak Crest Street after Whitney High School founding principal Robert
  Beall, pursuant to the City's Facility Naming and Renaming Policy, to a future City
  Council meeting, to allow for the conduct of additional research on the matter and
  receipt of further community input (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  Monday, March 23, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 8 of 9

9.  New and Old Business

9B.  (continued)

  SUBSTITUTE MOTION (ADOPTED): It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by
  Pulido, to rename the intersection at Shoemaker Avenue and Oak Crest Street after
  Whitney High School founding principal, Robert Beall (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Yokoyama
  NOES:  Tse, Johnson
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending or existing legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  Reports

11A.  Report from City Manager/Executive Director

  None.

11B.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports

  Reports were given by Councilmembers Hong and Pulido, Mayor Pro Tem Johnson,
  and Mayor Yokoyama.

  As requested by Mayor Yokoyama, Cerritos Sheriff’s Station Captain, Dru Strong,

  CONSENSUS (Yokoyama): Directed the City Manager to prepare letters of
  gratitude (including information related to the City’s percentage of reduction in crime

  to the Cerritos Sheriff’s Station; each Cerritos Neighborhood Watch Captain; and to

  Pam Lee, City Attorney, announced the City Council would recess to Closed Session

  Significant exposure to litigation pursuant to paragraph (2) of subdivision (d)

  Number of potential cases: Two (2)

  The City Council recessed into Closed Session.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Pam Lee, City Attorney, announced the City Council convened into Closed Session to

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 11:59 p.m.
